## Record both cameras

Use an overlapping GoPro MP4 from each camera on the same rigid mount. Record
with GPMF telemetry enabled and identical recording settings. Switch
HyperSmooth off, especially when using a calibrated rig. A short, sharp twist
of the entire rig near the start and end helps the worker estimate timing and
clock drift. Keep the rig steady and move slowly during the survey.

OpenReef accepts one MP4 per camera, up to 50 GiB combined. Choose a matching
pair of clips when a survey is split into GoPro chapters. The original MP4s
retain the embedded telemetry used for synchronization.

## Configure & Run

1. Open **Configure & Run → Stereo video** and give the survey a name.
2. Choose the Camera A and Camera B MP4s. Set the physical camera used as the
   left/time-reference camera. On the CCMI rig, this is Camera B.
3. Choose an existing **rig.json** or select **Uncalibrated**.
4. Choose the sampling interval and maximum pair count. The default interval
   is one second. JPEG setting 2 is high quality and 1 is the highest setting.
   Optional underwater colour correction changes the colour of the extracted
   stills without resizing them.
5. Pick the RunPod runtime and select **Upload & run**. **Compact preview**
   produces the web model. **Full project + compact preview** also packages the
   dataset and can include the prepared JPEGs.
6. To inspect the stills first, enable **Pause for frame-pair review** before
   submitting. When Stage 0 finishes, download the paired frames and
   `pairs.csv`. Open corresponding left and right JPEGs side by side, check a
   sharp event, and enter the pair numbers to exclude. Select **Run
   reconstruction** with at least two pairs retained. With review disabled,
   reconstruction starts automatically after preparation.

### Use an existing rig profile

Use the profile for the same physical camera order, baseline, underwater
housings, lens mode, field of view and image resolution. The first camera in
the JSON must be the left/time-reference camera. Recalibrate after changing
the rig geometry or optical settings.

A compatible profile contains two camera IDs, pixel dimensions, camera
models, intrinsic parameters and the rigid transform `rightFromLeft`.
The transform satisfies `X_right = R X_left + t`, with translation in metres.
OpenReef uses the calibrated intrinsics and fixed relative pose in COLMAP.
The baseline provides metric scale. Profile selection uses a calibration
created previously. For instructions on making a checkerboard profile, see
the [existing stereo calibration workflow](../STEREO.md).

### Run uncalibrated

GoPro telemetry still aligns the images in time. COLMAP estimates camera
geometry from visual matches, with no fixed relative pose or shared-intrinsics
constraint across the two cameras. The reconstruction has arbitrary scale
unless you set scale from a suitable known-size reference. This option is
useful when you lack a profile or need a preliminary model.

## Watch Stage 0 and review synchronization

The **Camera A** and **Camera B** bars show their own upload percentage, bytes
and transfer rate. The API relays signed multipart requests to the RunPod
network volume. Both video objects must be complete and match the expected
sizes before the API queues the worker. The worker reads the mounted files
and rechecks their sizes before extracting frames.

If the browser closes or the connection drops, open the job in **Job history**,
reselect the original MP4s if prompted and choose **Resume uploads**. Completed
files are reused. Multipart uploads resume from the last committed chunk.

OpenReef reads the GoPro GPMF gyroscope packets, aligns angular-speed traces
and estimates a linear offset and drift. It selects the nearest actual video
presentation timestamp in the second camera for each sampled reference frame,
then checks the decoded frame timestamps. Both JPEGs in a pair are labeled
with the same time for reconstruction. Creation time, when present, labels
the reference clock only. Gyroscope data determines the alignment.

Check the Stage 0 downloads:

- `pairs.csv` lists the selected frame indices, original video times and
  signed nearest-frame residual. Frame indices are zero-based and pair
  numbers are one-based.
- `sync.json` records the reference camera, offset, drift, gyro fit quality,
  available stabilization and rolling-shutter metadata, and optical-flow
  and calibrated epipolar checks where those checks are conclusive.
- `timestamps.json` supplies the shared capture time for each left and right
  JPEG. The paired archive contains these sidecars and the full-size stills.

Treat a short or weak gyro fit, a large optical-flow discrepancy or high
epipolar error as a reason to inspect the paired images and the rig setup.
Nearest-frame pairs suit reconstruction. Precision stereo measurements of
moving targets require a workflow that accounts for exposure timing and
rolling shutter.

## Retrieve outputs

The job view refreshes automatically as RunPod publishes results. Individual
downloads appear under **Stage outputs** even before the final model is
complete. Enable **Automatically download available stage archives** to save
them while the job page is open. Browser download settings can require
permission for multiple files. Manual download links remain available.

| Stage | Saved output |
|:--|:--|
| 0. Upload & prepare | Paired stills and synchronization metadata |
| 1. Features and matches | COLMAP database and available matching diagnostics |
| 2. Sparse reconstruction | COLMAP model and available sparse point cloud |
| 3. Undistortion and OpenMVS import | Undistorted COLMAP dataset and OpenMVS scene |
| 4. Dense point cloud | OpenMVS dense scene and point clouds |
| 5. Surface mesh | Mesh files |
| 6. Texture mesh | Textured mesh outputs and the final GLB |

Use **Job history** to reopen the preparation and reconstruction logs or
download completed stages. After reconstruction, select **Download all results
locally**. Extract the archive and open `model.glb` in desktop OpenReef.
The archive also contains the stage archives and, if selected, the full
project package.

After opening the local archive and verifying the files you need, check
**I saved and opened the local results archive** and select **Purge this
job’s RunPod files**. RunPod removes the uploaded videos, project workspace,
logs and downloads for that job. A small history entry remains. Keep your
original MP4s and the downloaded archive locally. A failed job can be retried
with its uploaded videos and retained checkpoints.

## Start a local frontend

Use Node.js 22.13 or newer. From the OpenReefGPU directory:

```sh
npm ci
NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENREEF_API_URL=http://localhost:8787 npm run dev -- --port 3000
```

The local API and GPU worker setup is documented in
[RunPod volume deployment](RUNPOD_VIDEO_VOLUME.md). OpenReef v0.7 uses
cloud package version `0.6.5-gpu.12`
and keeps the pinned OpenReef 0.6.5 reconstruction engine. The API and GPU
image should use the same version. In the desktop workspace checkout, start
the app with `OPENREEF_CLOUD_URL` set to the frontend URL to show
**Configure & Run on RunPod** on the **Process** page.

Render this manual with `quarto render docs/openreef-user-manual.qmd`.
